issues.legal_issue: A small causes court may decide title incidentally in an eviction proceeding and should return the plaint only when the claimed relief depends on a final determination of title that it cannot make.
material_facts: The proceeding sought eviction of a tenant under the rent-control law, and the tenant disputed the claimant’s title and the landlord-tenant relationship.
The trial court had found that the claimant acquired the property through gifts and had inducted the tenant.
The title question could be considered incidentally, while final determination of title could be left to a competent court.
issues.conclusion: Returning the plaint under Section 23(1) was erroneous because final determination of title was not necessary to decide the eviction claim.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1) of the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 gives the small causes court discretionary power to return a plaint when the relief depends on proof or disproof of a title that the court cannot finally determine. That power should be exercised only when the relief cannot be granted without such final determination. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from premises.
predicates.title_question_can_be_decided_incidental: The court can consider the disputed title as an incidental issue while deciding the claim.
predicates.final_title_determination_not_necessary: The relief sought can be decided without finally determining title to the property.

issues.definition: When an eviction claim can be decided by considering title incidentally and does not require a final title determination, returning the plaint is unwarranted.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s denial of the landlord’s title does not by itself prevent a rent-control court from deciding an eviction proceeding, and denial of the landlady’s title may itself be a ground for eviction.
material_facts: The tenant had been inducted into the premises by the claimant’s predecessor in title.
The trial court found that the claimant had acquired the property by gift and that she was the tenant’s landlady.
The tenant denied the claimant’s title and refused to recognize her as landlady.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was liable to be evicted under Section 20(2)(f) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972, for denying the landlady’s title.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(2)(f) of the Uttar Pradesh Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 makes denial of the landlord’s title a ground for eviction. A tenant cannot avoid an eviction proceeding merely by denying the relationship of landlord and tenant. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding under rent-control law seeking eviction of a tenant.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_found: The court found that the claimant was the tenant’s landlord or landlady.
predicates.tenant_denied_landlord_title: The tenant denied the claimant’s title to the premises.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction proceeding, when the court finds a landlord-tenant relationship and the tenant denies the landlord’s title, eviction is warranted.

issues.legal_issue: Allegations that rented premises are evacuee or enemy property do not make an eviction proceeding unmaintainable when no competent authority has declared the premises to have that status.
material_facts: The tenant raised objections based on the Evacuee Property Act, 1950 and the Enemy Property Act, 1968.
The competent enemy-property authority investigated the complaint and discharged the notice after finding no enemy interest in the premises; that order was not challenged.
No material showed that a competent authority had declared the premises to be evacuee or enemy property.
issues.conclusion: The objections based on the evacuee-property and enemy-property laws did not prevent the eviction proceeding from being decided.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, absent a declaration by a competent authority in a duly constituted proceeding that the property was evacuee or enemy property, those objections had no significance for deciding the eviction proceeding. The Court considered the Evacuee Property Act, 1950 and the Enemy Property Act, 1968. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.rent_eviction_proceeding: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking eviction of a tenant from premises.
predicates.no_competent_property_status_declaration: No competent authority had declared the premises to be evacuee or enemy property in a duly constituted proceeding.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is pending and no competent authority has declared the premises to have the claimed special property status, that status objection does not bar the eviction proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A remand is unnecessary when the material findings supporting an eviction decree remain undisturbed and the small causes court need not finally determine title to decide the claim.
material_facts: The trial court found that the claimant owned the premises, had inducted the tenant, and was entitled to eviction.
The revisional court had not disturbed the trial court’s findings on the merits and had ultimately decreed eviction.
The High Court quashed the revisional order and remanded the matter for fresh decision, although final determination of title was not needed for the eviction proceeding.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s remand was unnecessary and its order was set aside; the revisional decree of eviction was confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, in the circumstances, the remand was unnecessary because the trial court’s findings on the merits had not been disturbed and title could be considered incidentally. It allowed the appeal and confirmed the revisional court’s eviction decree. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.challenge_to_eviction_order: A party challenged an order concerning an eviction decree, and the challenged decision had remanded the matter for fresh proceedings.
predicates.material_trial_findings_undisturbed: The findings supporting the eviction decree had not been set aside or disturbed on their merits.
predicates.final_title_determination_not_necessary: The eviction claim could be decided without finally determining title to the property.

issues.definition: When an eviction order is challenged, its material trial findings remain undisturbed, and final title determination is unnecessary, remand is unnecessary and the eviction decree is confirmed.
